what: Visualizing latent ancestral states on the tree
title: Ancestral state reconstruction
text: can paint tree estimated ancestral values mapping posterior median diverging color gradient. Blue indicates low latent values; red indicates high: plot chunk asr-latent-tree
code: tree <- attr(asr_latent, "ref_tree") n_tips <- length(tree$tip.label) asr_all <- coev_ancestral_states(fit, nodes = "all")  pal <- colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "#F7F7F7", "#B2182B"))(100) rng <- range(asr_all$estimate)  # helper: map values onto the palette to_color <- function(x) {   pal[pmax(1, pmin(100, findInterval(x, seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 101))))] }  par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(2, 0, 2, 0))  for (var in unique(asr_all$variable)) {   vals <- setNames(asr_all$estimate[asr_all$variable == var],                    asr_all$node[asr_all$variable == var])   plot(tree, show.tip.label = FALSE, edge.width = 1.5,        edge.color = "grey70", main = gsub("_", " ", var))   internal_ids <- (n_tips + 1):(n_tips + tree$Nnode)   nodelabels(pch = 21, bg = to_color(vals[as.character(internal_ids)]),              col = NA, cex = 1.2) }  # shared color bar par(fig = c(0.35, 0.65, 0.02, 0.18), new = TRUE, mar = c(1.8, 0, 1.1, 0)) image(seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 100), 1,       matrix(1:100), col = pal, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "") axis(1, cex.axis = 0.7, padj = -1, tck = -0.25) mtext("Latent eta", side = 3, line = 0.2, cex = 0.7)

code: cat_labels <- c("Absent", "Sublocal", "Local", "Supralocal") cat_colors <- c("#FFFFB2", "#FECC5C", "#FD8D3C", "#E31A1C") n_cats <- length(cat_labels)  # pivot ordinal-response long format -> per-node probability matrix to_pie_mat <- function(df) {   wide <- df |>     select(node, category, estimate) |>     pivot_wider(names_from = category, values_from = estimate) |>     arrange(node)   mat <- as.matrix(wide[, paste0("cat_", seq_len(n_cats))])   mat / rowSums(mat) }  par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 0, 3, 0))  for (var in unique(asr_resp$variable)) {   df_var <- asr_resp |> filter(variable == var)   plot(tree, show.tip.label = FALSE, edge.width = 1.5,        edge.color = "grey50", main = gsub("_", " ", var))   # internal nodes: model-estimated category probabilities   nodelabels(pie = to_pie_mat(filter(df_var, node > n_tips)),              piecol = cat_colors, cex = 0.6)   # tips: observed value (deterministic) when present, otherwise model estimate   tip_pie <- to_pie_mat(filter(df_var, node <= n_tips))   obs <- authority$data[[var]][match(tree$tip.label, authority$data$language)]   observed <- !is.na(obs)   tip_pie[observed, ] <- 0   tip_pie[cbind(which(observed), as.integer(obs[observed]))] <- 1   tiplabels(pie = tip_pie, piecol = cat_colors, cex = 0.4) }  # shared legend par(fig = c(0.2, 0.8, 0, 0.12), new = TRUE, mar = rep(0, 4)) plot.new() legend("center", legend = cat_labels, fill = cat_colors, xpd = NA,        horiz = TRUE, bty = "n", cex = 0.9, title = "Authority level")

title: Introduction to the coevolve package
text: coevolve package, main function coev_fit(), fits generalized dynamic phylogenetic model traits given phylogenetic relationships among taxa. model allows user determine whether evolutionary change one trait precedes evolutionary change another trait. hood, package estimates parameters following stochastic differential equation along branches phylogenetic tree. equation partitions evolutionary change traits state-dependent deterministic selection state-independent Brownian motion, similar multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process: \[ d\pmb{\eta}(t) = (\textbf{}\pmb{\eta}(t) + \textbf{b}) + \textbf{G}dW(t) \] \(\pmb{\eta}(t)\) vector latent variables time \(t\). matrix \(\textbf{}\) represents “selection” strictly negative autoregressive terms diagonal. -diagonals may positive negative, controlling effect trait others (e.g., \(\textbf{}[2,1]\) represents effect \(\eta_1\) \(\eta_2\)). \(\textbf{b}\) vector continuous time intercepts. matrix \(\textbf{G}\) Cholesky decomposition positive semi-definite “drift” covariance matrix \(\textbf{Q}\) scales Brownian motion process \(W(t)\). following observation-level measurement model links \(\pmb{\eta}\) observations tips tree: \[ \begin{split} y_{[n,j]} \sim f(\mu_{[n,j]}, {\phi}_{[j]}) \\ g(\mu_{[n,j]}) = \pmb{\eta}_{[n]} \end{split} \] \(y_{[n,j]}\) denotes observed value trait \(j\) species population \(n\) tips phylogeny. \(f()\) probability density mass function expected value \(\mu\) additional distributional parameters \(\pmb{\phi}\). \(g()\) denotes link function, transforms expected value support function \(f()\) latent values unbounded continuous space evolutionary process. Similar dynamic coevolutionary models offered programs like BayesTraits (see ). However, models limited small number discrete traits. coevolve package goes beyond models allowing user estimate coevolutionary effects number variables much wider range response distributions, including continuous, binary, ordinal, count distributions. information model, refer introductory methods paper .
